title: AWS opens its first Asia Pacific region in Singapore
description: Amazon Web Services launched its Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region, its first in the region.
significance: Made Singapore the region's first cloud hub, a decade before Johor.

title: Google's first Singapore data centre begins operations in Jurong West
description: Google's first Singapore data centre began operating in 2014, followed by a second in 2015, both in Jurong West.
significance: Start of the hyperscale era in Singapore and its western data centre cluster.
source_name: Straits Times via Asia News Network

title: Alibaba Cloud opens its first Singapore data centre
description: Alibaba Cloud set up its Singapore data centre in Sept 2015 to serve Southeast Asia and added a second availability zone in June 2016.
significance: Singapore became the first overseas base for China's largest cloud; it is still Alibaba's regional hub.

title: Facebook announces S$1.4bn Tanjong Kling data centre
description: Facebook (now Meta) announced a US$1bn (S$1.4bn), 11-storey data centre at Tanjong Kling sized at 150 MW in 30 MW phases, its first in Asia, with phase 1 targeted for 2022.
significance: The largest single hyperscale build announced before the moratorium.

title: Government imposes an informal moratorium on new data centres
description: In 2019 Singapore began a review of the data centre industry and paused approvals for new data centres. Data centres used about 7% of electricity (3.4 TWh) in 2020.
significance: Turned scarcity into policy: the pause pushed new hyperscale demand across the border to Johor and Batam.

title: Global Switch opens Woodlands data centre with China Telecom Global and Daily-Tech
description: Global Switch, whose largest shareholder by then was China's Jiangsu Shagang group (49.9% per DCD), opened a S$280m, 25,000 m2 Woodlands facility in partnership with China Telecom Global and Daily-Tech.
significance: An early example of Chinese capital and carriers in Singapore's data centre stock. Amount is S$280m converted at about 0.74 (our arithmetic).

title: Moratorium lifted with a selective regime
description: Trade minister Gan Kim Yong said the review was complete and new capacity would be more selective, favouring best-in-class efficiency. About 70 DCs with roughly 1,000 MW were installed, using about 7% of national electricity.
significance: Replaced the pause with rationing by application rather than open entry.

title: First LTMS-PIP power trade from Laos to Singapore
description: Up to 100 MW of Lao hydropower began flowing to Singapore via Thailand and Malaysia under a two-year deal among EdL, EGAT, TNB and Keppel Electric.
significance: First multilateral power trade in ASEAN and Singapore's first renewable import; a pathfinder for the ASEAN Power Grid.

title: Google opens third Singapore data centre
description: Google opened its third Jurong West data centre, taking its Singapore investment to US$850m.
significance: Hyperscalers kept building on land and power secured before the pause.
source_name: Straits Times via Asia News Network

title: Indonesia extends Corridor (Grissik) piped gas to Singapore to 2028 at lower volumes
description: Indonesia agreed to extend the Corridor Block gas export contract to Singapore, due to expire in 2023, by five years to 2028, with volumes SKK Migas estimated 30 to 40% lower to prioritise domestic demand.
actor: SKK Migas; ConocoPhillips Grissik; Repsol; Pertamina
significance: Signalled that Singapore's cheap piped gas from Sumatra is winding down and LNG will fill the gap.

title: Princeton Digital launches SG+ with 96 MW Batam campus
description: Singapore-based PDG announced its SG+ strategy so customers can expand from Singapore into Batam and Johor, starting with a 96 MW, roughly US$1bn campus in Nongsa Digital Park, about 20 km from Singapore.
significance: Made the 'Singapore plus' spillover model explicit: Singapore sells the network, neighbours supply the megawatts.

title: Pilot DC-CFA awards about 80 MW to four bidders
description: EDB and IMDA provisionally awarded about 80 MW under the pilot Data Centre Call for Application to AirTrunk-ByteDance (consortium), Equinix, GDS and Microsoft, chosen from more than 20 proposals. Winners had to meet Green Mark DC Platinum and use liquid cooling and efficient IT.
significance: First new capacity after the 2019 to 2022 pause, and a template for rationed, auctioned-by-merit power.

title: EMA conditionally approves 2 GW of Indonesian power imports
description: EMA conditionally approved five projects for 2 GW of low-carbon imports from Indonesia (later licensed in Sept 2024), aiming for commercial operation from 2028.
significance: First large tranche of the import strategy; relies on Riau solar plus storage and subsea cables.

title: Carbon tax rises from S$5 to S$25 per tonne
description: Singapore's carbon tax rose to S$25/tCO2e for 2024 to 2025, then to S$45 from 1 Jan 2026, with a goal of S$50 to 80 by 2030.
significance: Raises the cost of gas-fired power that data centres draw from the grid.

title: Malaysia launches ENEGEM for green power sales to Singapore
description: Malaysia set up Energy Exchange Malaysia (ENEGEM) to auction green electricity to Singapore licensees under its cross-border sales scheme; registration opened 16 April 2024.
actor: Malaysia Ministry of Energy Transition (PETRA); Single Buyer
significance: Malaysia reversed its 2021 ban on renewable exports and opened a channel for Singapore buyers.

title: AWS pledges S$12bn more in Singapore by 2028
description: AWS said it would invest an additional S$12bn in Singapore cloud infrastructure from 2024 to 2028, on top of S$11.5bn through 2023.
significance: Largest single hyperscaler pledge for Singapore; USD figure is our conversion.

title: Green Data Centre Roadmap frees at least 300 MW
description: IMDA's roadmap provides at least 300 MW of extra capacity in the near term, mainly from efficiency gains, plus potentially 200 MW or more through green energy deployments. DCs used 7% of electricity; all DCs to reach PUE 1.3 or better within 10 years.
significance: Formalised the rule that growth must come from efficiency and green energy, not plain grid power.

title: Google completes fourth Singapore data centre
description: Google's fourth Singapore data centre took its total infrastructure investment to US$5bn from US$850m in 2022.
significance: Increment computed by us; shows hyperscalers keep expanding inside the rationed market.

title: Import target raised from 4 GW to 6 GW by 2035
description: EMA raised the low-carbon import goal to about 6 GW by 2035, licensed 2 GW of Indonesian projects and conditionally approved 1.4 GW more (Singa Renewables 1 GW; Shell-Vena 0.4 GW).
significance: Imports would be about a third of 2035 demand (NCCS); the main path to power data centres without more gas.

title: EMA conditionally approves Australia-Asia PowerLink
description: EMA granted conditional approval for SunCable's AAPowerLink to deliver 1.75 GW from Northern Territory solar, about 15% of Singapore's needs (company claim).
significance: Longest-reach import proposal; no operating date given.

title: First 50 MW ENEGEM sale from TNB to Sembcorp
description: TNB signed to supply 50 MW of renewable power to Sembcorp Power over the existing interconnector, starting December 2024; the scheme targets up to 300 MW.
significance: First Malaysian green power export to Singapore.

title: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone agreement exchanged
description: Leaders exchanged the JS-SEZ pact (signed 6 Jan) covering over 3,500 km2 across nine Johor zones incl. Sedenak, with 11 sectors including digital economy and energy and targets of 100 projects and 20,000 jobs in ten years. Data centres not named; both sides will facilitate renewable trade.
significance: Formalises the Singapore-Johor split: Singapore headquarters and network, Johor land and power. Sedenak is Johor's main data centre cluster.

title: US AI Diffusion Rule puts compute caps on most countries
description: The Biden administration's rule capped AI compute exports to Tier 2 countries; Tier 1 firms could place at most 7% of compute in any one Tier 2 country. It was rescinded on 13 May 2025 before compliance began.
significance: Singapore and Malaysia were not Tier 1, so the rule threatened AI builds there; the rescission opened a window that Chinese-linked firms reportedly used.

title: Nvidia filing shows 18% of revenue billed to Singapore but under 2% shipped there
description: Nvidia's annual report showed Singapore at 18% of FY2025 revenue (about US$24bn) by billing location, but under 2% (about US$473m) shipped to Singapore. Nvidia said customers centralise invoicing in Singapore.
significance: Fed suspicion that Singapore was a conduit for chips to China; Nvidia's stated explanation is invoicing.

title: Three men charged over server fraud reportedly linked to Nvidia chips
description: Singapore charged two Singaporeans and a Chinese national with fraud against Dell and Super Micro by misrepresenting servers' final destination. The minister said servers went to Malaysia and may contain Nvidia chips; prosecutors later cited US$390m of transactions. Charges are allegations pending trial.
significance: Singapore's first public enforcement case on AI hardware diversion.

title: Sembcorp ends Mako piped gas deal after Indonesian approvals fail
description: Sembcorp Gas terminated its Sept 2023 agreement for up to 111 BBtu/d of piped gas from the Mako fields because it failed to receive Indonesian approvals.
significance: New piped supply from Indonesia is hard to secure; Singapore leans on LNG.

title: DayOne breaks ground on 20 MW Jurong data centre with fuel cells
description: DayOne, Singapore-based and formerly GDS International, broke ground on its 20 MW pilot DC-CFA facility at 21 Jalan Buroh in Jurong, planned as Singapore's first DC with on-site solid oxide fuel cells; phase 1 ready in 2026.
significance: Turns the GDS DC-CFA win into a build under a Singapore-headquartered entity.

title: AirTrunk raises US$1.8bn loan for 70 MW SGP2 in Loyang
description: AirTrunk, owned by Blackstone and CPP Investments, secured US$1.8bn from 20+ banks for SGP2, a 70+ MW campus in Loyang.
significance: Largest Singapore DC financing in our set; the AirTrunk-ByteDance DC-CFA link to this site is not confirmed.

title: NYT reports US Commerce probe of Singapore's Megaspeed
description: The New York Times reported Commerce officials were investigating whether Singapore-based Megaspeed, with close ties to Chinese tech firms, helped them evade US export controls; it was set to buy about US$2bn of Nvidia technology. Allegations; Megaspeed says it complies with export rules.
significance: Moved scrutiny from smuggling cases to cloud firms renting compute to Chinese clients.

title: Jurong Island to host 20 ha green data centre park of up to 700 MW
description: JTC and EDB set aside about 20 ha of Jurong Island for Singapore's largest low-carbon DC park, able to provide up to 700 MW, alongside 300 ha for new energies including hydrogen-ready gas and ammonia power.
significance: Moves future data centre growth onto the petrochemical island, beside gas and future hydrogen and ammonia.

title: Second call for application (DC-CFA2) launched for at least 200 MW
description: EDB and IMDA opened DC-CFA2 for at least 200 MW. Bidders must hit PUE 1.25 or better at full IT load, Green Mark DC 2024 Platinum, and power at least 50% of new capacity from green pathways such as biomethane, low-carbon ammonia or hydrogen, fuel cells with carbon capture or building-integrated solar.
significance: Tied new capacity to on-island green fuel pathways, not just grid power, and pushed AI-ready compute as a stated goal.

title: Singtel's Nxera opens 58 MW DC Tuas
description: Nxera opened an eight-storey 58 MW AI-ready facility in Tuas with direct-to-chip liquid cooling and a cable landing station; over 90% pre-committed. Nxera's Singapore capacity rose to 120 MW.
significance: Largest new Singapore-owned build; Nxera also expanding to Batam and Johor.

title: Qatar LNG to Singapore halted by Middle East war
description: Qatari LNG shipments to Singapore stopped in April 2026. Qatar had supplied about 48% of Singapore's 2025 LNG (3.2 Mt). EMA and GasCo secured US, Australian and African cargoes through end 2026; renewing consumers faced 5 to 10% higher power prices.
significance: Showed how a 93% gas grid exposes every Singapore data centre to LNG shocks.

title: BIS reaffirms licences for China-parented buyers anywhere
description: BIS guidance confirmed that since November 2023 advanced AI chips sent to any entity whose ultimate parent is in China or Macau need a US licence wherever the entity sits, and let existing operators keep chips already installed. Reports said the guidance aimed at Chinese firms building compute in Singapore and Malaysia.
significance: Reaffirmed the rule that matters most for Chinese-owned cloud and data centre tenants in Singapore.

title: DC-CFA2 awards 200 MW on Jurong Island to four operators
description: Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia Global Data Centres each got a provisional 50 MW, from more than 20 proposals. All four will be sited on Jurong Island; each must source over 50% of capacity from green energy. Agencies will review the need for a third call in 18 to 24 months.
significance: Largest single allocation since the moratorium, and all of it went to colocation landlords, three of them with Singapore or US roots, none Chinese.

title: DayOne files for US IPO
description: Singapore-headquartered DayOne (ex-GDS International) filed for a US IPO; reports say up to US$5bn at about US$20bn valuation. It had about 2.3 GW booked, mostly due by end-2028.
significance: A Singapore HQ lets a China-origin platform raise US capital for Johor and Batam capacity.

title: GasCo launches first term LNG tender; supply gap flagged
description: Singapore GasCo launched its first term LNG procurement as Singapore faces a gas gap of about 3 Mt in 2028 to 2029 rising to about 6 Mt by 2035. Indonesia cut piped exports by 31 MMscfd; a third LNG terminal on Pulau Tekong is under study.
significance: The gas that powers Singapore's data centres is increasingly bought on world LNG markets.

title: NYT reports US probe of Megaspeed executive; Nvidia CEO calls ties normal
description: The New York Times reported the US is investigating a Megaspeed executive for allegedly providing information to the Chinese government. Jensen Huang said Nvidia's dealings were 'normal' and it had counted every GPU deployment. China called the allegations a smear. Allegations, no charges reported.
significance: Turned a chip-control story into a counter-intelligence story centred on a Singapore-registered firm.

title: Equinix opens SG6
description: Equinix opened SG6, its sixth Singapore IBX and first built under the DC-CFA: up to 20 MW IT, design PUE 1.20, initial US$290m.
significance: First pilot DC-CFA allocation to start operating.

title: Reports allege Megaspeed moved US$7.5bn of Nvidia chips via Singapore and Malaysia
description: The Information reported at least US$7.5bn of Nvidia chips moved through Megaspeed and its Malaysian unit Speedmatrix (NYT: 200+ restricted shipments Jun 2024 to Jun 2025), some to data centres serving Alibaba and Tencent. Singapore says it is investigating Megaspeed for suspected breaches of domestic law; Nvidia's board opened an independent review on 8 Nov. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. All allegations.
significance: The largest alleged diversion case linked to Singapore; puts the hub's trust model at risk.
